messages.author: bc810b1d0900407f
messages.subject: A strange behavior of equal()
parts:
Hi All,

I have never used equal() in mode syntax, as far as I can recall. Using labels is much more convenient. However, I am working on something that may require me to work with it, and I came across a strange behavior.

This is the example:

``` r
library(lavaan)
#> This is lavaan 0.6-16
#> lavaan is FREE software! Please report any bugs.

mod1 <-
"
x4 ~ x1 + x2 + x3
x5 ~ a * x1 + equal('x5 ~ x1') * x2
"

fit1 <- sem(mod1, data = HolzingerSwineford1939)
parameterEstimates(fit1)[c(4, 5), ]
#>   lhs op rhs label   est    se     z pvalue ci.lower ci.upper
#> 4  x5  ~  x1     a 0.306 0.064 4.798  0.000    0.181    0.430
#> 5  x5  ~  x2 x5~x1 0.063 0.063 0.993  0.321   -0.061    0.186

mod2 <-
"
x4 ~ x1 + x2 + x3
x5 ~ x1 + equal('x5 ~ x1') * x2
"

fit2 <- sem(mod2, data = HolzingerSwineford1939)
parameterEstimates(fit2)[c(4, 5), ]
#>   lhs op rhs label   est    se     z pvalue ci.lower ci.upper
#> 4  x5  ~  x1  .p4. 0.183 0.038 4.832      0    0.109    0.258
#> 5  x5  ~  x2 x5~x1 0.183 0.038 4.832      0    0.109    0.258
```

<sup>Created on 2023-09-24 with [reprex v2.0.2](https://reprex.tidyverse.org)</sup>

In the first version, I expect  "x5 ~ a * x1 + equal('x5 ~ x1') * x2" will make the paths "x5 ~ x1" and "x5 ~ x2" equal. However, it is not the case, as shown in the parameter estimates.

If I remove the label, then equal() works as expected, as shown in the second version.

I checked the parameter tables:

Version 1:

   id lhs op rhs user block group free ustart exo label plabel  start   est
4   4  x5  ~  x1    1     1     1    4     NA   0     a   .p4.  0.306 0.306
5   5  x5  ~  x2    1     1     1    5     NA   0 x5~x1   .p5.  0.063 0.063

Version 2:

   id  lhs op  rhs user block group free ustart exo label plabel  start   est
4   4   x5  ~   x1    1     1     1    4     NA   0  .p4.   .p4.  0.306 0.183
5   5   x5  ~   x2    1     1     1    5     NA   0 x5~x1   .p5.  0.063 0.183
15 15 .p4. == .p5.    2     0     0    0     NA   0               0.000 0.000

In the first version, equal() added 'x5~x1' as a label to 'x5~x2'. However, if 'x5~x1' is also labelled manually, the equality constraint is not added.

Moreover, when I fitted the first version, there was no warning message. 

I don't know whether this can be considered a bug. Or is equal() not intended to be used with labelled parameters? If this is the case, how about adding a warning message or even raising an error?

Regards,
Shu Fai

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: A strange behavior of equal()
parts:
On 9/24/23 02:58, Shu Fai Cheung wrote:
> x5 ~ a * x1 + equal('x5 ~ x1') * x2

This will fail indeed, as the 'a' label overwrites the 'automatic' label
'x5 ~ x1'. It would be nice indeed if this triggers a warning, but I
don't see how this can be done using the current implementation of the
syntax parser in lavaan (lavParseModelString()). Only the 'labels' are
saved, and afterwards, we cannot check which one was the result of equal().

Perhaps I should remove equal() altogether in a future update...

Yves.
